mainTopic: Which suspected wives (סוטה) drink and keep their כתובה, who can give the קינוי, and the sources for the ארוסה and שומרת יבם
overview: The משנה finishes its list of women in forbidden marriages, who neither drink the bitter water nor collect their כתובה. It then teaches that if the woman herself blocks the test, she loses her כתובה, but if her husband blocks it, she keeps it. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about a husband who died before his wife drank. The משנה adds disputed cases: a woman pregnant with or nursing another man's child, and a woman who cannot have children. All other women either drink or lose their כתובה, and even a כהן's wife and a סריס's wife drink. The משנה then teaches whom a husband can warn his wife about, and when the בית דין gives the קינוי in his place. The גמרא learns from a פסוק that an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם can receive a קינוי even though they do not drink. It shows that the משנה follows רבי יונתן against רבי יאשיה and explains their reasoning. It then begins to explain what רבי יונתן learns from 'איש איש', a list that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Women in forbidden marriages neither drink nor collect
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of forbidden marriages: a נתינה married to a regular ישראל, or a בת ישראל married to a ממזר or a נתין. These women do not drink the bitter water and do not collect their כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נתינה married to a ישראל, and a בת ישראל married to a ממזר or a נתין: they do not drink and do not collect a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list that began on the previous daf. The list covers couples whose marriage is forbidden, and its ruling is that the wife neither drinks nor collects her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These marriages are forbidden, so the סוטה process of testing the wife with the water does not apply to them. Because the marriage itself is forbidden, she also does not receive her כתובה payment.

keyTerms.meaning: A descendant of the גבעונים, who may not marry into regular Jewish families
A child born from a forbidden union, who may not marry a regular Jew
They drink (the bitter water of the סוטה)
The marriage contract money a wife collects when the marriage ends

steps.confusionAlert: This list did not start here. It began on the previous daf with cases like an אלמנה married to a כהן גדול. These lines are just the end of that list.

phrases.english: and a Gibeonite woman married to a Jew,
and a Jewish woman married to a mamzer or a Gibeonite —
they neither drink nor collect their marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of forbidden marriages from the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In forbidden marriages, the wife does not drink and does not collect her כתובה.

steps.title: Confession, witnesses, or refusal to drink
steps.stepSummary: Three women neither drink nor collect their כתובה: one who admits she is defiled, one against whom witnesses testify, and one who refuses to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: These women do not drink and do not collect a כתובה: a woman who says 'I am טמאה,' a woman who has witnesses that she is טמאה, and a woman who says 'I will not drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new list: women who lose both the drinking and the כתובה because of something on their side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water is only for a case of doubt. If she confesses or witnesses testify, there is no doubt left, so there is nothing to test. If she refuses to drink, she is the one blocking the test, so she loses her כתובה even without confessing.

keyTerms.meaning: I am defiled (she admits she was unfaithful)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the main idea for the next step: when the woman is the cause of not drinking, she loses her כתובה.

phrases.english: And these do not drink
and do not collect their marriage contract:
a woman who says, "I am defiled,"
and one about whom witnesses came that she is defiled,
and a woman who says, "I will not drink."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ לֹא שׁוֹתוֹת וְלֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from forbidden marriages to cases where the woman herself ends the process
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Confession, witnesses, or refusal to drink means she neither drinks nor collects her כתובה.

steps.title: When the husband blocks the test, she keeps her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: If the husband refuses to have her drink, or he lived with her on the way, she does not drink but she does collect her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her husband said 'I will not make her drink,' or her husband was with her on the way, they collect the כתובה and do not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite case. Here the husband is the reason she cannot drink, so she still collects her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compare this with Step 2. There, the woman stopped the test and lost her כתובה. Here, the husband stopped it, by refusing or by living with her on the way, so she does not lose her money.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not make her drink
He lived with her as husband and wife
On the way (to the בית המקדש)

steps.whatToRemember: Who stopped the drinking? If it was the woman, she loses her כתובה. If it was the husband, she keeps it.

phrases.english: If her husband said, "I will not make her drink,"
and one whose husband lived with her on the way —
phrases.notes: 'On the way' means on the trip to the בית המקדש, where the drinking would take place.

phrases.english: they collect their marriage contract and do not drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to Step 2: here the husband causes the non-drinking
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband prevents the drinking, the wife collects her כתובה.

steps.title: Husband died before she drank: בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree
steps.stepSummary: If the husband died before the wife drank, בית שמאי say she collects her כתובה and does not drink. בית הלל say she either drinks or does not collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husbands died before the women drank: בית שמאי say they collect the כתובה and do not drink. בית הלל say they either drink or do not collect their כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת. A husband dies before his suspected wife drinks. Does she still get her כתובה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that she was never proven guilty, so she collects her כתובה without drinking. בית הלל hold that her right to the כתובה depends on clearing herself. If she does not drink, the doubt stays, and she does not collect.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not take בית הלל's 'or they drink' at face value yet. The גמרא later asks how a woman can drink at all once her husband is no longer alive.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: she collects without drinking. בית הלל: no drinking means no כתובה.

phrases.english: If their husbands died before they drank,
Beit Shammai say:
they collect their marriage contract and do not drink,
and Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שׁוֹתוֹת אוֹ לֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתוּבָּתָן.
phrases.english: either they drink, or they do not collect their marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case: neither husband nor wife blocked the test, but the husband died
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: she collects without drinking. בית הלל: she drinks, or she does not collect.

steps.title: A woman pregnant or nursing from another man
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a man who marries a woman pregnant with or nursing another man's child is in a forbidden marriage, so she neither drinks nor collects her כתובה. חכמים say he can separate from her and take her back later, so the marriage is not in that category.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman pregnant from another man, or nursing another man's baby, does not drink and does not collect her כתובה. This is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים say: he can separate from her and take her back after the waiting time is over.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case to its list of forbidden marriages, and חכמים argue about whether it belongs there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats this marriage like the forbidden ones in Step 1, so she cannot drink and loses her כתובה. חכמים say the problem is only temporary: he can separate from her now and remarry her later. So for them it is not a truly forbidden marriage, and she can drink.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman pregnant with another man's child
A woman nursing another man's child

phrases.english: A woman pregnant from another man
and a woman nursing another man's child
neither drink nor collect their כתובה,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the Sages say:
He is able to separate from her
and take her back after the time has passed.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Could be split into a מימרא of רבי מאיר and a מחלוקת response of חכמים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of forbidden marriages begun in Step 1, now with a disputed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: no drinking and no כתובה. חכמים: since he can separate and remarry her later, the marriage is not forbidden, so she can drink.

steps.title: A woman who cannot have children
steps.stepSummary: An איילונית, an elderly woman, and any woman unable to give birth neither collect their כתובה nor drink. רבי אלעזר says the husband can marry another woman and have children through her, so this marriage is acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: An איילונית, an old woman, and a woman who cannot give birth do not collect their כתובה and do not drink. רבי אלעזר says: he can marry another woman and have children through her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another disputed case: a husband who married a woman who cannot bear children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion sees this marriage as blocking the מצוה of פרו ורבו, so it counts as forbidden, and she cannot drink. רבי אלעזר answers that the husband can still fulfill the מצוה with another wife. So this marriage is not a problem, and she drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who never physically matures and cannot bear children
To have children (the מצוה of פרו ורבו)

phrases.english: An איילונית and an elderly woman,
phrases.notes: An איילונית is a woman whose body never fully developed, so she can't have children.

phrases.english: and a woman who is not able to give birth
neither collect their כתובה nor drink.
רבי אלעזר says:
He is able to marry another woman
and be fruitful and multiply through her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 5: a disputed case of whether a marriage counts as forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: no כתובה and no drinking. רבי אלעזר: since he can have children with another wife, the marriage is fine and she drinks.

steps.title: All other women, a כהן's wife, and a סריס's wife
steps.stepSummary: Every woman not on the list either drinks or gives up her כתובה. A כהן's wife drinks and, if found innocent, stays permitted to him. A סריס's wife also drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: All other women either drink or do not collect their כתובה. A כהן's wife drinks and is permitted to her husband. A סריס's wife drinks.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes the list with a general rule for everyone else, then names two special husbands whose wives still drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any normal, permitted marriage goes by the rule 'either drink or lose the כתובה'. A כהן's wife is not excluded even though a כהן has stricter marriage rules. Once the water shows she is innocent, she may stay with him. A סריס's wife also drinks, even though he cannot have children.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who cannot father children

steps.whatToRemember: The default rule for any permitted marriage: the wife either drinks or loses her כתובה. Only the special forbidden marriages are exempt from drinking.

phrases.english: And all the other women

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שׁוֹתוֹת אוֹ לֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתוּבָּה.
phrases.english: either drink or do not collect their כתובה.
The wife of a כהן drinks
and is permitted to her husband.
The wife of a סריס drinks.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁאָר כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים אוֹ שׁוֹתוֹת אוֹ לֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of exceptions by stating the general rule for every other woman, then adds two special cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All other wives drink or lose their כתובה. A כהן's wife and a סריס's wife both drink.

steps.title: Which men a husband can warn his wife about
steps.stepSummary: A husband can give the warning (קינוי) about any man, even a relative she is forbidden to, except for a minor and 'one who is not a man', meaning an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: A husband may warn his wife about any forbidden relative, except about a minor and about one who is not a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to a new question: about whom a husband can give his wife the warning that starts the סוטה process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think he cannot warn her about her father or brother, since they are forbidden to her anyway. The משנה says he can. The warning does not work for a minor or for 'one who is not a man'.

keyTerms.meaning: Give the warning (קינוי) not to be alone with a certain man
Relatives a person is forbidden to have relations with
A minor, a boy under בר מצוה age
One who is not a man (an animal)

steps.whatToRemember: The warning works even for forbidden relatives, but not for a minor or an animal.

phrases.english: One may give the warning about all forbidden relatives,
except for a minor
and for one who is not a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who drinks to a new topic: about whom the warning (קינוי) can be given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קינוי works for any man, even forbidden relatives, but not for a minor or an animal.

steps.title: The court warns when the husband cannot
steps.stepSummary: If the husband became a חרש or a שוטה, or is in prison, the בית דין gives the קינוי in his place. The תנא קמא says this warning only takes away her כתובה. It does not lead to drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the women the court warns: one whose husband became deaf-mute, became mentally incompetent, or is in prison. The warning is not meant to make her drink. It is only meant to take away her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה names three situations where the husband cannot warn his wife himself, so the בית דין does it for him. It then limits what that warning accomplishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only the husband gives the קינוי. Here the בית דין steps in. According to the תנא קמא, the result is smaller: if she secludes herself after the warning, she loses her כתובה, but she does not go through the ritual of the bitter water.

keyTerms.meaning: To make her lose the right to her כתובה

phrases.english: And these are the women to whom the court gives the warning:
one whose husband became a deaf-mute,
or became mentally incompetent,
or was locked up in prison.
They did not say this in order to make her drink,
but rather to take away her כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's discussion of קינוי. Step 8 covered whom the husband can warn about. This step covers when the court warns in his place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband cannot warn, the בית דין warns. According to the תנא קמא, this only takes away her כתובה and does not lead to drinking.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the court's warning can lead to drinking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the court's warning also counts for drinking. When the husband gets out of prison, he can make her drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says the warning is also for drinking. When her husband leaves prison, he makes her drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the תנא קמא and gives the court's warning its full force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the court's קינוי is as strong as the husband's own. His example is the prisoner, who can later bring her to the ritual himself. The disagreement is only about whether a warning given by the court can lead to drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: To make her drink the bitter water

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says a קינוי from the court only costs her the כתובה. רבי יוסי says it can also lead to drinking once the husband is released from prison.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: also to make her drink.
When her husband comes out of prison, he makes her drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא of step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court's warning also counts for drinking. The husband can make her drink after his release.

steps.title: They do not drink, but can they be warned? What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier ruling that an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם do not drink. It infers that they can still receive a קינוי, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only drinking is what she does not do, but he can still warn her. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from the משנה's wording, then asks for its source. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said these women 'do not drink'. It did not say they cannot be warned. The precise wording implies that a קינוי still works on them, so if she secludes herself she becomes forbidden to him. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
From where are these things learned?
A betrothed woman, not yet living with her husband
A widow waiting for her brother-in-law to do יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as being about the court's warning from step 9. The גמרא is going back to an earlier line of the משנה about the ארוסה and the שומרת יבם.

phrases.english: Gemara
It is only drinking that she does not do,
phrases.notes: This is about the ארוסה and the שומרת יבם, whom the משנה said do not drink.

phrases.english: but he can give her a warning:
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets just fixes the spelling; the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: From where are these things learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with an inference from an earlier line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם can receive a קינוי.

steps.title: The extra words 'and say' include them in the warning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'דבר אל בני ישראל ואמרת' that an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם are included in the laws of קינוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Speak to the children of Israel and say.' This comes to include a betrothed woman and a widow waiting for יבום in the warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא that brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the extra word 'ואמרת' as coming to add something. What it adds is the ארוסה and the שומרת יבם, but only for קינוי, not for drinking. So the warning works on them even though they never reach the bitter water.

keyTerms.meaning: For the laws of the warning

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'Speak to the children of Israel and say'
this comes to include a betrothed woman and a widow waiting for יבום in the warning.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'ואמרת' includes an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם in the laws of קינוי.
steps.whatToRemember: An ארוסה and a שומרת יבם do not drink, but a קינוי does work on them.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יונתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the author of the משנה, which says that neither the ארוסה nor the שומרת יבם drinks. It is רבי יונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose opinion is our משנה? It is רבי יונתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows and answers right away: רבי יונתן. The next steps bring the ברייתא that shows why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה excludes both women from drinking. That only fits a תנא who excludes both, so the גמרא needs to find who holds that way. The proof comes next.

phrases.english: And our משנה, whose opinion is it?
It is Rabbi Yonatan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the קינוי rule back to the משנה's ruling that these women do not drink, and identifies its author.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה excludes only the ארוסה
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי יאשיה learns from 'תחת אישך' that an ארוסה does not drink. He learns from 'איש איש' that a שומרת יבם does drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Under your husband' excludes a betrothed woman. You might think I also exclude a widow waiting for יבום, so the פסוק says 'any man'. These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens with רבי יאשיה's view. It is set up as the contrast to רבי יונתן, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ארוסה does not yet live 'under' her husband, so she is excluded. The double word 'איש איש' adds the שומרת יבם back in, so for רבי יאשיה she drinks. That cannot match our משנה, which says she does not drink.

keyTerms.meaning: Any man (literally 'a man, a man'), which adds a case

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Under your husband'
excludes a betrothed woman.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא אַף שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם,
phrases.english: You might think I also exclude a widow waiting for יבום,
so the פסוק says: 'any man',
these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that supports step 13 by first giving the opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יאשיה: an ארוסה does not drink, but a שומרת יבם does.

steps.title: רבי יונתן excludes both women
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן learns from 'תחת אישך' that a שומרת יבם does not drink. He learns from the second פסוק, 'תחת אישה', that an ארוסה does not drink. This matches the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: 'Under your husband' excludes a widow waiting for יבום. You might think I exclude her but not a betrothed woman, so the פסוק says 'when a wife goes astray while under her husband'. This excludes a betrothed woman.
steps.whatsHappening: This completes the proof that the משנה follows רבי יונתן, since he excludes both women from drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן uses two separate פסוקים, one for each woman, so neither one drinks. That is exactly what the משנה rules, so the משנה must follow him and not רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יאשיה says only the ארוסה does not drink. רבי יונתן says both the ארוסה and the שומרת יבם do not drink. Our משנה follows רבי יונתן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says: 'Under your husband'
excludes a widow waiting for יבום.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹצִיא שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם וְלֹא אוֹצִיא אֶת אֲרוּסָה,
phrases.english: Should I exclude a widow waiting for יבום but not exclude a betrothed woman?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׂטֶה אִשָּׁה תַּחַת אִישָׁהּ״
phrases.english: So the פסוק says: 'when a wife goes astray while under her husband'
this excludes a betrothed woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second view in the ברייתא, which proves the identification made in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי יונתן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי יונתן excludes both the שומרת יבם and the ארוסה from drinking.

steps.title: Why רבי יונתן sees the ארוסה as more strongly bound
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן holds that an ארוסה is more firmly bound to the man than a שומרת יבם. She has his own קידושין, and she gets סקילה if she sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage (רבי יונתן) thinks the ארוסה is the stronger case, because the קידושין are his own, and she is stoned on his account.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why רבי יונתן and רבי יאשיה read the פסוקים differently. It starts with רבי יונתן's view that the ארוסה has the stronger bond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ארוסה was married through this man's own קידושין. A שומרת יבם is tied to him only through his brother's marriage. Also, an ארוסה who sins gets סקילה, which shows a serious bond. So for רבי יונתן, the plain exclusion 'תחת אישך' removes the weaker case, the שומרת יבם, and the ארוסה needs its own second פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They stone (the death penalty of סקילה)
On his account, because of her tie to him

steps.confusionAlert: 'Stronger bond' does not mean this woman is more likely to drink. For רבי יונתן, neither woman drinks. The question is only which one the main פסוק excludes and which one needs an extra source.

phrases.english: One Sage holds the betrothed woman is stronger,
phrases.notes: This first Sage is רבי יונתן, and the other one is רבי יאשיה.

phrases.english: since the betrothal is his own,
and she is stoned on his account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יונתן's reading in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יונתן, the ארוסה has the stronger bond: she has his own קידושין and is liable to סקילה.

steps.title: Why רבי יאשיה sees the שומרת יבם as more strongly bound
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה holds that a שומרת יבם is more firmly bound, because she does not need חופה to complete the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other Sage (רבי יאשיה) thinks the שומרת יבם is the stronger case, because she is not missing entry into the חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side: רבי יאשיה's reason for treating the שומרת יבם as the stronger case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ארוסה still has a step left before full marriage: being brought to the חופה. A שומרת יבם has no such step, because יבום itself completes the marriage. So for רבי יאשיה, 'תחת אישך' excludes only the weaker case, the ארוסה, and 'איש איש' includes the שומרת יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: Being handed over to the חופה (the wedding canopy)
A widow waiting for her brother-in-law to do יבום

steps.whatToRemember: Each side picks a different woman as the 'stronger' case. רבי יונתן says the ארוסה, because the קידושין are his own and she gets סקילה. רבי יאשיה says the שומרת יבם, because she needs no חופה. The main exclusion 'תחת אישך' always removes the weaker case.

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds the widow awaiting her yavam is stronger,
since she does not lack being brought to the wedding canopy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the pair by giving רבי יאשיה's reasoning from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יאשיה, the שומרת יבם has the stronger bond, since she needs no חופה.

steps.title: What does רבי יונתן learn from 'איש איש'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה used 'איש איש' to include the שומרת יבם. רבי יונתן excludes her, so the גמרא asks what he uses that phrase for.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יונתן, what does he do with this phrase 'איש איש'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what extra lesson 'איש איש' teaches according to רבי יונתן. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doubled words like 'איש איש' are usually read as coming to include something. רבי יאשיה used it to include the שומרת יבם, but רבי יונתן says she does not drink. So the phrase seems unused in his view, and the גמרא needs to find another lesson for it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yonatan, this phrase "any man,"
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן, הַאי אִישׁ אִישׁ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the reasoning settled, the גמרא turns to the phrase that only רבי יאשיה has used so far.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יונתן learns from the doubled phrase 'איש איש'.

steps.title: 'איש איש' includes the wives of a חרש and a שוטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן needs 'איש איש' to include the wife of a חרש, the wife of a שוטה, and more. The list continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to include the wife of a deaf-mute, the wife of a שוטה, and the wife of…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי יונתן, 'איש איש' comes to include women whose husbands cannot give a קינוי themselves. The list carries on to the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש or a שוטה cannot legally give the warning on his own. Even so, 'איש איש' teaches that their wives are part of the laws of סוטה. So the phrase is not wasted for רבי יונתן; it simply includes different women.

phrases.english: He needs it to include
the wife of a deaf-mute, and the wife of an imbecile, and the wife of

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'איש איש' includes the wives of a חרש, a שוטה, and others in the laws of סוטה.
